subject: Post-demo follow-up: DPA path, SCC module preference, and VSQ kickoff
messages:
From: Michael Grant <michael.grant@redwood.ai>
To: Samir Khanna <samir@blueharbor.ai>, Lena Ortiz <lena.ortiz@blueharbor.ai>
Cc: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.ai>, Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 4 Nov 2026 15:10:00 -0500
Subject: Post-demo follow-up: DPA path, SCC module preference, and VSQ kickoff

Thanks for the time today — appreciate the deep dive on your routing workload and privacy posture. I wanted to capture the quick post-demo items and propose next steps so legal/procurement can pick this up cleanly.

Recap (short):
- BlueHarbor confirmed EU + US user base; GDPR in-scope for EU residents.
- You expect Redwood to act as the processor for the ML inference path; BlueHarbor is the controller.
- You requested our SOC 2 status, DPA steps, and guidance on SCC module choices.
- You'd like us to complete/host the Vendor Security Questionnaire (VSQ) so procurement can start the intake.

Immediate asks / next steps for BlueHarbor:
1) Confirm controller/processor: please confirm in writing that BlueHarbor intends to be the controller and Redwood the processor (one-line reply is fine).
2) Fill out the VSQ (link below) or attach an initial version — procurement wants any partial answers to triage effort.
3) Let us know if you need a specific SCC module (if your legal already prefers a module, tell us which).

What's coming from Redwood (I attached these):
- redwood_dpa_request_template.pdf (fillable DPA intake we use to streamline legal redlines)
- redwood_soc2_summary_2026.pdf (summary & scope; full report available under NDA)
- VSQ link: https://drive.google.com/redwood/vsq-template (we can pre-fill sections if you prefer)

Proposed timeline:
- You confirm controller/processor by end of week (11/6)
- You drop the VSQ back to me or upload to the drive by 11/9
- Legal-to-legal call (if needed) the week of 11/15

If that all sounds right I'll loop in our contracts lead and propose a short legal checklist for the DPA redline. Thanks again — happy to jump on a 20-min call if any of this needs clarifying.

Best,
Michael Grant
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
A: +1 (415) 555-0194 | michael.grant@redwood.ai

Attachments: redwood_dpa_request_template.pdf, redwood_soc2_summary_2026.pdf
From: Samir Khanna <samir@blueharbor.ai>
To: Michael Grant <michael.grant@redwood.ai>
Cc: Lena Ortiz <lena.ortiz@blueharbor.ai>
Date: Thu, 5 Nov 2026 09:22:00 -0500
Subject: Re: Post-demo follow-up: DPA path, SCC module preference, and VSQ kickoff

Thanks Michael — useful summary. A couple quick clarifications from our side:

- Confirmed: BlueHarbor will be controller; Redwood will be processor for all inference traffic that touches EU data. We'll put that in an email thread to legal as well.
- SOC 2: we saw your summary, thanks. We are currently collecting SOC 2 reports for vendors; you mentioned Type II is in progress. Can you share the expected completion quarter? A SOC bridge letter or summary will help for now.
- SCC module: our legal prefers to see a processor-first module (their baseline is Module 2) but they're open to Redwood's recommendation if you can map the modules to responsibilities (data export, subprocessors, DSR handling).

We started the VSQ; procurement asked us to send any partial answers ASAP so they can score vendors. I'll attach what we have by Friday. Also, can you confirm whether Redwood supports redaction for logs containing PII and what the retention defaults are for KV cache? That will be in the questionnaire.

Proposed next: I'll route to legal & procurement once I have the SOC details and your DPA template filled in. 11/9 for the VSQ is fine.

—Samir
Director, Security & Compliance
BlueHarbor Analytics
From: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.ai>
To: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.ai>, Michael Grant <michael.grant@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 5 Nov 2026 11:02:00 -0500
Subject: Fwd: BlueHarbor follow-up — quick internal notes (do not externalize)

Forwarding Samir's reply with notes for our playbook:

- Samir confirmed controller role — good, we can proceed with standard Processor DPA.
- SOC2 Type II timing: we should offer a SOC bridge + summary now; full Type II planned Q2 2027 per infra roadmap.
- SCC module preference: they mentioned Module 2 (processor-first). Recommend we propose Module 2 + a processor addendum that clarifies subprocessors and DSR handling (short form).
- VSQ: Offer to pre-fill sections for performance and infra, and ask legal to own data flow answers where decisions required.

Action items for us:
1) Michael to send DPA intake + prefilled VSQ link and attach SOC summary (I'll draft the short processor addendum language and loop in legal).
2) Jordan to prepare a one-pager mapping SCC Module 2 to Redwood responsibilities (single slide).

I'll coordinate with legal to get the addendum ready; propose "legal-to-legal" on 11/16 to resolve open redlines.

—Monica
Director, Customer Success Ops
From: Michael Grant <michael.grant@redwood.ai>
To: Samir Khanna <samir@blueharbor.ai>, Lena Ortiz <lena.ortiz@blueharbor.ai>
Cc: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.ai>, Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 6 Nov 2026 09:48:00 -0500
Subject: Re: Post-demo follow-up: DPA path, SCC module preference, and VSQ kickoff

Samir — thanks for the quick turn. Per Monica's notes, attaching the DPA intake we use to capture the fields legal needs (redwood_dpa_request_template.pdf) and a short SOC 2 summary (redwood_soc2_summary_2026.pdf). A few direct answers to your VSQ items:

- SOC 2 Type II: expected completion Q2 2027. In the interim we can provide a SOC bridge letter and the summary attached. If you need the full report we can provide via NDA.
- Logs & PII: Our default telemetry redaction removes full-text PII from request logging; we retain minimal request metadata for 30 days in hosted by default; dedicated/private customers can configure retention policies. We'll note this in the VSQ prefill.
- KV cache retention: default is 0 between requests unless customer enables persistent cache. We'll include clear options in the prefill.

SCC / DPA guidance:
- Recommendation: SCC Module 2 (processor-first) + short processor addendum clarifying subprocessors, DSR process, and breach notification SLA (48 hours initial notice). This maps to what Samir's legal asked for.

Links / attachments:
- DPA intake: https://app.redwood.ai/dpa-request/BH-2026-091 (fillable form)
- VSQ template: https://drive.google.com/redwood/vsq-template (we prefilled infra & ops sections)
- redwood_dpa_request_template.pdf (attached)
- redwood_soc2_summary_2026.pdf (attached)

If that looks good please confirm controller/processor in writing and upload any partial VSQ answers. I'll get our contracts lead to hold 11/16 15:00 ET for a legal-to-legal if they need it.

Best,
Michael
Account Executive, Redwood Inference

Attachments: redwood_dpa_request_template.pdf, redwood_soc2_summary_2026.pdf
From: Samir Khanna <samir@blueharbor.ai>
To: Michael Grant <michael.grant@redwood.ai>
Cc: Lena Ortiz <lena.ortiz@blueharbor.ai>
Date: Sat, 6 Nov 2026 10:23:00 -05:00
Subject: Re: Post-demo follow-up: DPA path, SCC module preference, and VSQ kickoff

Thanks — got everything and appreciate the clear mapping. I attached our in-progress VSQ (BH_vsq_partial_answers.xlsx); procurement will add scoring notes. Confirmed: BlueHarbor = controller, Redwood = processor (this thread suffices).

Next: I'll route the DPA intake + attachments to our legal and procurement. They should be able to review the prefilled VSQ and respond with clarifying questions by 11/12. If things look standard we'll aim for a short legal call on 11/16; please have your contracts lead on standby.

—Samir
Director, Security & Compliance
BlueHarbor Analytics

Attachments: BH_vsq_partial_answers.xlsx
